title: Lemon Harvesting
summary: One lemon and six limes are fixed to the front face of a wall in front of the hovering aerial manipulator, and a grey storage tote sits on a small table against the wall to the robot's left. Harvest the lemon: free it from the wall and get it into the tote. Success needs the lemon's reference point (the base of the fruit) inside the tote's nominal box while the gripper is fully open.
scene: The ground is the world's z = 0 plane. In front of the robot stands an immovable (kinematic) wall: a slab 0.1 m thick, 2.0 m wide and 2.0 m tall with a concrete-block surface, its front face turned toward the robot. The wall is the same in every instance. Seven fruits sit on its front face, each with its long axis pointing at the robot: one yellow lemon (about 7.6 x 5 x 5 cm, 50 g) and six green limes (about 7.6 x 6 x 6 cm). The limes are fixed in place and cannot be moved. The lemon is a free rigid body held to the wall by a breakable fixed joint: it stays put until the joint has to carry more than 10 N of force or 10 N m of torque, after which it is loose and falls under gravity. Where the fruits sit varies between instances: anywhere in a band 1 m wide and 0.4 m tall, centred sideways on the wall in its upper half, at least 15 cm apart. To the robot's left, against the wall, stands a small table (white top, about 0.45 x 0.48 m and 0.66 m tall) carrying an open-top grey plastic tote, 40 x 30 x 17 cm; table and tote are immovable and the same in every instance. Nothing moves by itself. The robot starts hovering level and motionless, facing the wall, with its arm at its zero joint configuration (end effector a little ahead of and above the airframe) and the gripper closed.
scene_privileged: One environment; its origin is the world origin. Robot at every reset: base_link at (0, 0, 1.0) m with orientation (1, 0, 0, 0) wxyz (body +x is the world +x direction), zero velocity; arm_link1_pitch_joint = arm_link2_pitch_joint = arm_link3_pitch_joint = arm_link4_roll_joint = 0 rad; arm_lfinger_joint = arm_rfinger_joint = 0.001 m (their lower limit: gripper closed, gripper_width 0.002 m). By the robot's URDF kinematics this puts ee_link at about (0.227, 0, 1.124) m with identity orientation and the tool-tip point (ee_link origin + 0.18 m along the ee_link x axis) at about (0.407, 0, 1.124) m; the end-effector command is initialised to the current ee_link pose. Wall: kinematic cuboid 0.1 (x) x 2.0 (y) x 2.0 (z) m, centre (2.0, 0.0, 1.0) m, orientation identity (front face x = 1.95, normal -x), not randomized; friction 1.0 / 1.0, restitution 0; visual material NVIDIA Concrete_Block.mdl. At each reset AM-Bench's randomize_wall_fruit_attachments puts the lemon's root at (1.92, y, z) with y ~ U(-0.5, 0.5) m, z ~ U(1.1, 1.5) m, then draws each of the six limes from the same distribution, rejecting draws closer than 0.15 m in (y, z) to the lemon or an earlier lime (up to 200 tries, else an error); identity orientations, zero velocity. A fruit's root is its body origin at the bottom of the fruit as authored: the lemon collider spans x +-0.038, y +-0.025, z 0.001..0.052 m about it, a lime x +-0.038, y -0.028..0.033, z 0..0.060, so every fruit occupies x 1.882..1.958, its far end 8 mm inside the wall. Lemon: lemon.usd, whose geometry is a payload (NVIDIA SimReady prop lemon_01, 'RigidBody' variant, convex-decomposition collider, SimReady 'organic' physics material: static friction 5.0, dynamic 0.9, restitution 0.001) referenced from NVIDIA's omniverse-content-staging server; dynamic, gravity on, mass 0.05 kg (mass_props). It hangs on a UsdPhysics fixed joint lemon_wall_fixed_joint (body0 the wall, localPos0 (0, 0, 0); body1 the lemon, localPos1 = the wall centre in the lemon frame, (0.08, -y, 1 - z); break force 10 N, break torque 10 N m), redefined at every reset. Limes: lime.usd, payload SimReady lime01 from the same server, same physics material, kinematic (mass 0.02 kg, no effect). Table: cline.usd, payload SimReady 'cline' table from the same server (white top, grey underside, wood legs, metal feet; convex-decomposition colliders with wood / metal physics materials), kinematic, scale (0.4, 0.2, 0.8), body placed at (1.72, 0.5, 0.0) at each reset: it occupies x 1.497..1.944, y 0.258..0.741, z 0..0.656. Container: container.usd, whose geometry is a payload (NVIDIA warehouse asset Container_B06_40x30x17cm, 'Gray' variant, convex decomposition) from NVIDIA's content server, kinematic, scale (1, 1, 1), root (the tote's bottom centre) at (1.72, 0.5, 0.65) at each reset, identity: the tote spans x 1.52..1.92, y 0.35..0.65, z 0.65..0.82. AM-Bench's lemon_pos and container_pos observations are these roots. Scene default physics material: friction 1.0 / 1.0, restitution 0.
success: Success at a control step when both hold: (1) the lemon's root position (its body origin, at the bottom of the fruit in the lemon's own frame) is inside, bounds inclusive, the world-axis-aligned box container_root + [(-0.20, -0.15, 0), (0.20, 0.15, 0.17)] m, i.e. the tote's nominal 0.40 x 0.30 x 0.17 m size above its bottom-centre root; (2) the gripper width, arm_lfinger_joint + arm_rfinger_joint (each limited to [0.001, 0.045] m, so 0.002 to 0.09 m in total), is > 0.0898 m (gripper_open_threshold): both fingers essentially at their open limit. The lemon need not be at rest and its orientation is not tested; being inside the box at one step is enough. AM-Bench also reports lemon_grasped_and_detached (latched once lemon and tool tip have moved together >= 0.02 m with the gripper closed below 0.05 m and the lemon within 0.12 m of the tool tip) and lemon_delivered_released (the success itself); they are informational only. Evaluated after every control step (decimation 1, so after every 1/120 s physics step) on the simulated state; no hold time is required. The episode terminates at the first step where it holds. Otherwise it is truncated by the time limit: episode_length_s = 30 s, i.e. max_episode_length = 3600 control steps; AM-Bench raises the time-out when episode_length_buf >= max_episode_length - 1, i.e. at the 3599th step.
difficulty_note: The lemon has to be told apart from six fixed limes, freed from a joint that only gives way under a 10 N load, carried to the tote and let go with the gripper fully open, all from a hovering base; the fruits' places on the wall change per instance.
standard_notes: The fruits' positions, which fruit is the lemon, the tote's and table's poses and whether the lemon is still attached are not given: the yellow lemon has to be told from the green limes and located on the concrete wall with the onboard cameras, and the tote found on the table. The gripper width comes from proprioception; whether the lemon is in the tote can only be judged visually. Success is not reported during the episode.
